tool_input.content:
# Plan: Coherent three-level table of contents

## Context

The TOC behaviour is currently incoherent, and `CONTENTS:` depth is a no-op.

Three structural markers exist, but they collide and behave inconsistently:

| Marker | Today's LaTeX | In TOC today? |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| `=== Title ===` (Section) | `\section*` | **No** — never registered |
| `** Q1 **` (Solution) | `\section*` | Yes (always) |
| `(a)` (Part) | `\subsection*` | Only if `--toc-parts` CLI flag set |

Two defects:

1. **`===` and `**` both render `\section*`** — they occupy the same level, so a
   section cannot nest its questions.
2. **`CONTENTS:` depth (`\setcounter{tocdepth}`) is inert.** Every heading is
   *starred* plus a manual `\addcontentsline`. `\addcontentsline` writes to the
   `.toc` unconditionally; `tocdepth` only gates the *automatic* entry an
   *unstarred* `\section` would make. We never emit unstarred sectioning, so
   `tocdepth` changes nothing. `CONTENTS: full` therefore renders identically to
   `CONTENTS:`. (Confirmed by LaTeX semantics; the new tests assert the
   mechanism directly via `\addcontentsline` presence/absence.)
3. **Parts can only enter the TOC via a CLI flag** — the document has no
   self-contained way to control its own TOC content.

**Intended outcome:** three markers map to three distinct native levels; every
marker can appear in the TOC; `CONTENTS:` depth is a real, document-driven knob
that *filters which `\addcontentsline` calls are emitted* (not `tocdepth`).

User decision (recorded): **three native levels**, accepting that `**`/`(a)`
headings render one step smaller and committed `.tex`/`.pdf` regenerate.

## Design of record

Level mapping (display command = TOC level, so heading size encodes nesting):

| Marker | Heading | TOC level | Emitted when |
|--------|---------|-----------|--------------|
| `=== Title ===` | `\section*` | `section` | depth ≥ 1 (always) |
| `** Q1 **` | `\subsection*` | `subsection` | depth ≥ 2 |
| `(a)` (subsection mode) | `\subsubsection*` | `subsubsection` | depth ≥ 3 **or** `toc_parts` |

Depth is a generator-side filter on `\addcontentsline` emission. `CONTENTS:`
keyword → depth:

- empty → `1` (sections only)
- `2` → `2` (sections + questions)
- `3` → `3` (sections + questions + parts)
- `full` / `all` → `3` (all levels) — **note: `full` now means 3, was 2**

`--toc-parts` is retained as an **override**: it forces part-level entries even
when depth < 3. (`if self._toc_depth >= 3 or self.toc_parts`.)

`PARTS: inline` mode parts produce no heading and never enter the TOC —
unchanged.

Out of scope for jms: this is typographic/document hierarchy, not Z notation,
schema calculus, or fuzz acceptance.

## Files to modify

### Engine — delegate to **rmh** (TDD, `make check` clean)

- **`src/txt2tex/latex_gen.py`** — in `generate_document()` (entry ~line 390,
  loop ~line 480), add a pre-scan over `ast.items` for the first `Contents`
  node before the main generation loop. Map its `.depth` keyword → int via a new
  helper `_toc_depth_from_keyword(value: str) -> int`. Store on
  `self._toc_depth`. **Default = 3** when no `Contents` node (harmless: no
  `\tableofcontents` renders the entries). Initialise `self._toc_depth` in
  `__init__` (near `toc_parts`, line ~171).
- **`src/txt2tex/codegen/text_blocks.py`**:
  - `_generate_section` (46-61): add
    `\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{<escaped title>}` after `\section*`.
    Guard `if self._toc_depth >= 1` (always true; kept for symmetry).
  - `_generate_solution` (63-77): `\section*` → `\subsection*`; addcontentsline
    level `section` → `subsection`; guard `if self._toc_depth >= 2`.
  - `_generate_part` subsection branch (257-260): `\subsection*` →
    `\subsubsection*`; addcontentsline level `subsection` → `subsubsection`;
    guard `if self._toc_depth >= 3 or self.toc_parts`.
  - `_generate_contents` (370-387): keep `\tableofcontents`; set
    `\setcounter{tocdepth}{<n>}` to the numeric depth (documents intent though
    inert for starred headings). Reuse the same `_toc_depth_from_keyword` helper
    so the keyword→int map has one source.

Reuse `self._escape_latex_text` (already used at `text_blocks.py:53`) for the
section title in `\addcontentsline`.

### Tests — **rmh**, written first and shown failing before implementation

Generator unit tests (assert on exact fragments, not substring presence):

- Heading commands: `===` → `\section*{...}`; `**` → `\subsection*{...}`;
  `(a)` (subsection mode) → `\subsubsection*{(a)}`.
- Section now registered: `\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{...}` present.
- Depth filter:
  - `CONTENTS:` (1): section line present; subsection (solution) absent;
    subsubsection (part) absent.
  - `CONTENTS: 2`: section + subsection present; subsubsection absent.
  - `CONTENTS: 3` and `CONTENTS: full`: all three present.
- `--toc-parts` override: depth 1 + `toc_parts=True` → part
  `\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}` present.

Add an integration fixture exercising `=== ` + `**` + `(a)` + `CONTENTS: full`
together (none currently combines all four). Place under `examples/user_guide/`
or a dedicated `examples/` subdir; commit `.txt` + regenerated `.tex`.

### Fixtures — **adb** (toolchain) after engine is green

- `make regen-e2e` regenerates all `examples/**/*.tex`. Review `git diff
  examples/` — expect every doc with `**`/`(a)` to change (smaller headings,
  new/section addcontentsline). Rebuild affected `.pdf` via `examples/Makefile`.
- Regenerate `tests/bugs/**/*.tex` fixtures that contain these markers.
- Regenerate `hw1/solutions.tex` + `.pdf`.

### Docs — **ghr**

- `docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md` — rewrite the `CONTENTS:` section: keyword→depth
  table, the three-level hierarchy, the `**`/`(a)` size change, `--toc-parts` as
  override. Update the summary in `CLAUDE.md` "Input Format" if it states TOC
  behaviour.
- `docs/DESIGN.md` — add an ADR: rejected "keep `**` at section / `===` at
  part"; chose three native levels; rationale that `tocdepth` is inert with
  starred headings so depth must filter `\addcontentsline`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under `## [Unreleased]` — note the behaviour change
  (`**`/`(a)` heading sizes, sections now in TOC, `full` now = all levels).

### CLI — **mdm** (small)

- `src/txt2tex/cli.py:192-196` — update `--toc-parts` help to state it is now an
  override that forces parts into the TOC regardless of `CONTENTS:` depth.

### Security — **djb**: skip. No subprocess/path/untrusted-input surface changes.

## Verification (end-to-end)

1. Engine: `make check` green (mypy, pyright, ruff, format, tests, coverage).
2. Run CLI on `hw1/solutions.txt` (uses `** **` + `(a)` + bare `CONTENTS:`):
   confirm `.tex` shows `\subsection*` for questions and section-only TOC
   entries; build PDF, `pdftotext -`, confirm TOC lists questions only.
3. Run CLI on the new `===`/`**`/`(a)`/`CONTENTS: full` fixture: build PDF,
   inspect the TOC page visually — confirm three-level nesting (section ▸
   question ▸ part) and that heading sizes descend with depth.
4. Smoke a Z example (e.g. `examples/10_schemas/`) through fuzz via the z-spec
   `check` tool to confirm no regression in unrelated output.
5. `make regen-e2e`; review `git diff examples/`; confirm every change is the
   expected size/registration shift and nothing unrelated moved.

## Open product call (confirm or override)

`full` is redefined from depth 2 → depth 3 (all levels). Bare `CONTENTS:`
(depth 1, the common case incl. `hw1`) is unaffected. Say the word to keep
`full` = 2 instead.

"""Tests for three-level table-of-contents heading hierarchy.

Covers: Section (===), Solution (**), Part (subsection mode) heading
commands and addcontentsline emissions, plus depth filtering via
CONTENTS: keyword and _toc_depth_from_keyword.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from txt2tex.latex_gen import LaTeXGenerator, _toc_depth_from_keyword
from txt2tex.lexer import Lexer
from txt2tex.parser import Parser


def _latex(src: str, **kwargs: bool) -> str:
    """Parse src and return generated LaTeX body."""
    lexer = Lexer(src)
    tokens = lexer.tokenize()
    ast = Parser(tokens).parse()
    gen = LaTeXGenerator(**kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return gen.generate_document(ast)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _toc_depth_from_keyword unit tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestTocDepthFromKeyword:
    """Unit tests for the keyword-to-depth mapping."""

    def test_empty_string_gives_1(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("") == 1

    def test_2_gives_2(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("2") == 2

    def test_3_gives_3(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("3") == 3

    def test_full_gives_3(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("full") == 3

    def test_all_gives_3(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("all") == 3

    def test_full_case_insensitive(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("FULL") == 3

    def test_all_case_insensitive(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("ALL") == 3

    def test_2_with_whitespace(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("  2  ") == 2

    def test_unrecognised_gives_1(self) -> None:
        assert _toc_depth_from_keyword("unknown") == 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Heading command tests (the *starred* heading that appears in output)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestSectionHeadingCommand:
    r"""=== Title === must emit \section*{…}."""

    def test_section_emits_section_star(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("=== Introduction ===\n")
        lines = latex.splitlines()
        assert r"\section*{Introduction}" in lines

    def test_section_emits_addcontentsline(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("=== Introduction ===\n")
        lines = latex.splitlines()
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Introduction}" in lines


class TestSolutionHeadingCommand:
    r"""** Q1 ** must emit \subsection*{…} (not \section*{…})."""

    def test_solution_emits_subsection_star(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("** Q1 **\n\nx = 1\n")
        lines = latex.splitlines()
        assert r"\subsection*{Q1}" in lines

    def test_solution_emits_addcontentsline_at_subsection(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("** Q1 **\n\nx = 1\n")
        lines = latex.splitlines()
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in lines

    def test_solution_does_not_emit_section_star(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("** Q1 **\n\nx = 1\n")
        # \section* must not appear for a solution marker
        assert r"\section*{Q1}" not in latex


class TestPartHeadingCommand:
    r"""(a) in subsection mode must emit \subsubsection*{…}."""

    def test_part_emits_subsubsection_star(self) -> None:
        # Top-level part (no enclosing solution) triggers subsection mode
        latex = _latex("(a) Some content\n")
        lines = latex.splitlines()
        assert r"\subsubsection*{(a)}" in lines

    def test_part_emits_addcontentsline_at_subsubsection(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("(a) Some content\n")
        lines = latex.splitlines()
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in lines

    def test_part_does_not_emit_subsection_star(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex("(a) Some content\n")
        assert r"\subsection*{(a)}" not in latex


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Depth filter tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestDepthFilter:
    """CONTENTS: depth controls which addcontentsline calls are emitted."""

    _FULL_DOC = (
        "CONTENTS: {depth}\n"
        "\n"
        "=== Title ===\n"
        "\n"
        "** Q1 **\n"
        "\n"
        "(a) Part content\n"
    )

    def _latex_for_depth(self, depth_keyword: str) -> str:
        src = self._FULL_DOC.format(depth=depth_keyword)
        return _latex(src)

    def test_depth1_section_present(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Title}" in latex

    def test_depth1_subsection_absent(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" not in latex

    def test_depth1_subsubsection_absent(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" not in latex

    def test_depth2_section_present(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("2")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Title}" in latex

    def test_depth2_subsection_present(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("2")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in latex

    def test_depth2_subsubsection_absent(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("2")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" not in latex

    def test_depth3_all_present(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("3")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Title}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex

    def test_full_keyword_all_present(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("full")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Title}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex

    def test_all_keyword_all_present(self) -> None:
        latex = self._latex_for_depth("all")
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Title}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex


class TestDefaultDepth:
    """Without CONTENTS: in the document, default depth is 3 (emit everything)."""

    def test_no_contents_node_section_addcontentsline_present(self) -> None:

@item_register.register(Contents)
    def _generate_contents(self, node: Contents) -> list[str]:
        """Generate LaTeX for table of contents.

        CONTENTS: generates \tableofcontents (sections only, depth 1)
        CONTENTS: full generates \tableofcontents with depth 2 (sections + subsections)
        CONTENTS: 2 also generates \tableofcontents with depth 2
        """
        lines: list[str] = []
        # Determine depth: empty = 1 (sections only)
        # "full" or "2" = 2 (sections + subsections)
        if node.depth.lower() in ("full", "2"):
            lines.append(r"\setcounter{tocdepth}{2}")
        else:
            lines.append(r"\setcounter{tocdepth}{1}")
        lines.append(r"\tableofcontents")
        lines.append("")
        return lines

    """Return numeric TOC depth from a CONTENTS: keyword string.

    Maps: "1" → 1; empty / "2" / unrecognised → 2; "3" / "full" / "all" → 3.
    Bare CONTENTS: and unknown values default to 2 (sections + subsections).

tool_input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head feat/toc-levels --title "feat(toc): three-level table of contents with depth filtering" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Make the table of contents coherent. The three structural markers now map to three distinct LaTeX heading levels, so heading size encodes nesting and every marker can appear in the TOC:

| Input | Heading | TOC level |
|-------|---------|-----------|
| `=== Title ===` | `\section*` | section |
| `** Solution **` | `\subsection*` | subsection |
| `(a)` part | `\subsubsection*` | subsubsection |

Previously `===` and `**` **both** rendered `\section*` (collision — a section could not nest its solutions), and `===` sections never entered the TOC at all.

## Why depth is a generator-side filter

LaTeX's `\setcounter{tocdepth}` is **inert** here: every heading is starred plus a manual `\addcontentsline`, which writes to the `.toc` unconditionally. `tocdepth` only gates the *automatic* entry an *unstarred* `\section` makes, which txt2tex never emits. So `CONTENTS:` depth is enforced by filtering which `\addcontentsline` calls are emitted.

`CONTENTS:` keyword → depth:

| Keyword | Depth | Lists |
|---------|-------|-------|
| `CONTENTS:` (bare) | 2 | sections + solutions |
| `CONTENTS: 1` | 1 | sections only |
| `CONTENTS: 2` | 2 | sections + solutions |
| `CONTENTS: 3` / `full` / `all` | 3 | + parts |

Bare `CONTENTS:` defaults to depth 2 so the common solutions document lists its solutions with no extra syntax. `--toc-parts` is retained as a depth override.

## Behavior changes (breaking for output)

- `**` solutions render one level smaller (`\subsection*`), `(a)` parts one level smaller (`\subsubsection*`).
- `===` sections now appear in the TOC.
- `full` now means all levels (depth 3); was depth 2.

96 example `.tex` + 87 `.pdf` regenerated to match.

## Verification

- `make check` green (4795 passed, 3 expected xfails).
- Built PDFs for bare `CONTENTS:` (lists solutions), `CONTENTS: 1` (sections only), and `CONTENTS: full`; confirmed the rendered Contents page nests section ▸ solution ▸ part.
- Every changed `examples/*.tex` line verified to be a heading-level or `\addcontentsline` shift — no unrelated movement.

## Out of scope

`hw1/` fixtures are **not** regenerated: `hw1/solutions.txt:541` (`List ::= nil | join <<...>>`) hits an unrelated parse error — `join` now lexes as the relational-algebra keyword and breaks the free-type definition. Pre-existing on `main`; tracked separately.

## Delegation

rmh (engine + tests), mdm (CLI help), ghr (docs), adb (fixtures). jms not consulted — typographic hierarchy, not Z semantics.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

PR review (Copilot) found a real bug in the TOC work, and it stems from a wrong premise I gave you. I verified empirically: LaTeX `tocdepth` DOES gate display of manually-added `\addcontentsline` entries (compiled a doc with `tocdepth 1` + all three `\addcontentsline` levels present — only the section showed; subsection/subsubsection were hidden). So `tocdepth` is NOT inert. The TOC is gated by BOTH our emission filter AND `tocdepth`, and right now `--toc-parts` makes them disagree.

Two concrete defects:
1. `--toc-parts` (documented as a depth override → depth 3) only affects the part-emission guard. The pre-scan leaves `_toc_depth` at the keyword value, so `CONTENTS: 1` + `--toc-parts` emits parts but suppresses their parent solutions (guard `>= 2`) → orphaned subsubsection entries with no subsection parent.
2. `_generate_contents` sets `\setcounter{tocdepth}` from the raw keyword. With `--toc-parts` you emit subsubsection `\addcontentsline` but set tocdepth to 1/2 → LaTeX hides those entries in the printed TOC.

Fix (tie both mechanisms to one effective depth). Write-set: `src/txt2tex/latex_gen.py`, `src/txt2tex/codegen/text_blocks.py`, `tests/test_11_text_blocks/test_toc_three_levels.py`. TDD: update/add the failing tests first, show red, implement, show green, `make check` green.

1. `latex_gen.py` pre-scan (the loop that sets `self._toc_depth` from the first `Contents` node, ~line 481): AFTER that loop, add `if self.toc_parts: self._toc_depth = 3`. So `--toc-parts` raises the effective depth to 3 regardless of keyword (and regardless of whether a Contents node exists — default 3 already, so no-op there).

2. `text_blocks.py` `_generate_contents`: set the counter from the EFFECTIVE depth, i.e. `\setcounter{tocdepth}{<self._toc_depth>}` instead of recomputing `toc_depth_from_keyword(node.depth)`. `self._toc_depth` is set in the pre-scan before this runs, so it already reflects the `toc_parts` bump. Update the docstring to say tocdepth is set from the effective depth (keyword, raised to 3 when `--toc-parts`), and that the printed TOC is gated by BOTH `tocdepth` and the `\addcontentsline` emission, which now both derive from `self._toc_depth`.

3. `text_blocks.py` `_generate_part` subsection branch: the guard `if self._toc_depth >= 3 or self.toc_parts:` can now simplify to `if self._toc_depth >= 3:` (since `toc_parts` raises `_toc_depth` to 3). Make that simplification.

4. Tests:
   - Fix `TestTocPartsOverride`: drive it with `CONTENTS: 1` + `toc_parts=True` (not bare `CONTENTS:`). Assert: part `\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}` PRESENT; solution `\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{…}` ALSO present (override pulls solutions in too); and `\setcounter{tocdepth}{3}` present (override reflected in the rendered counter). Update the class docstring.
   - Add a contrast test: `CONTENTS: 1` WITHOUT `toc_parts` sets `\setcounter{tocdepth}{1}` and emits only the section `\addcontentsline` (no subsection/subsubsection).
   - Any existing test asserting `_generate_contents` tocdepth from keyword alone: confirm it still holds for the non-toc_parts path.

Report red→green evidence and confirm `make check` green. Do NOT touch docs — I'll correct the docs and PR body myself.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# toc_parts override
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestTocPartsOverride:
    """toc_parts=True raises effective depth to 3, keeping tocdepth consistent.

    Both the addcontentsline emission guards and \setcounter{tocdepth} derive
    from self._toc_depth, which is bumped to 3 when toc_parts is set.
    """

    _SRC = "CONTENTS: 1\n\n=== Title ===\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"

    def test_toc_parts_subsubsection_present(self) -> None:
        latex = _latex(self._SRC, toc_parts=True)
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex

    def test_toc_parts_subsection_present(self) -> None:
        # Override pulls solutions in too — no orphaned subsubsection entries
        latex = _latex(self._SRC, toc_parts=True)
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in latex

    def test_toc_parts_tocdepth_set_to_3(self) -> None:
        # \setcounter{tocdepth}{3} keeps the printed TOC consistent with emission
        latex = _latex(self._SRC, toc_parts=True)
        assert r"\setcounter{tocdepth}{3}" in latex

    def test_no_toc_parts_depth1_tocdepth_is_1(self) -> None:
        # Contrast: without override, CONTENTS: 1 → tocdepth 1
        latex = _latex(self._SRC)
        assert r"\setcounter{tocdepth}{1}" in latex

    def test_no_toc_parts_depth1_only_section_addcontentsline(self) -> None:
        # Contrast: without override, only section entry emitted
        latex = _latex(self._SRC)
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Title}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" not in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" not in latex

gh pr edit 66 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Make the table of contents coherent. The three structural markers now map to three distinct LaTeX heading levels, so heading size encodes nesting and every marker can appear in the TOC:

| Input | Heading | TOC level |
|-------|---------|-----------|
| `=== Title ===` | `\section*` | section |
| `** Solution **` | `\subsection*` | subsection |
| `(a)` part | `\subsubsection*` | subsubsection |

Previously `===` and `**` **both** rendered `\section*` (collision — a section could not nest its solutions), and `===` sections never entered the TOC at all.

## How depth works

The starred headings carry manual `\addcontentsline` calls. Two levers gate the printed TOC and must agree: which entries the generator writes, and LaTeX's `tocdepth`, which gates which written entries actually display (`\l@subsection` tests `\c@tocdepth`). txt2tex computes **one effective depth** and drives both from it — sets `\setcounter{tocdepth}` to it and omits `\addcontentsline` below it — so they cannot disagree.

`CONTENTS:` keyword → depth:

| Keyword | Depth | Lists |
|---------|-------|-------|
| `CONTENTS:` (bare) | 2 | sections + solutions |
| `CONTENTS: 1` | 1 | sections only |
| `CONTENTS: 2` | 2 | sections + solutions |
| `CONTENTS: 3` / `full` / `all` | 3 | + parts |

Bare `CONTENTS:` defaults to depth 2 so the common solutions document lists its solutions with no extra syntax. `--toc-parts` raises the effective depth to 3 (override), pulling parts — and their parent solutions — into the TOC regardless of the keyword. Parts in the TOC require subsection-mode parts (the default); `PARTS: inline` parts have no heading and are not listed.

## Behavior changes (breaking for output)

- `**` solutions render one level smaller (`\subsection*`), `(a)` parts one level smaller (`\subsubsection*`).
- `===` sections now appear in the TOC.
- `full` now means all levels (depth 3); was depth 2.

96 example `.tex` + 87 `.pdf` regenerated to match.

## Review fixes (Copilot)

A first cut rested on a wrong premise ("`tocdepth` is inert for starred headings"). Disproven by compiling a doc with `tocdepth 1` and `\addcontentsline` at all three levels — only the section showed. Copilot caught that `--toc-parts` consequently emitted part entries that `tocdepth` hid and orphaned their parent solutions. Fixed by deriving both levers from one effective depth (commit `d2a906c`); docs corrected.

## Verification

- `make check` green (4799 passed, 3 expected xfails).
- Built PDFs for bare `CONTENTS:` (lists solutions), `CONTENTS: 1` (sections only), `CONTENTS: full`, and `CONTENTS: 1 --toc-parts` — the last now correctly shows section ▸ solution ▸ part.
- Every changed `examples/*.tex` line verified to be a heading-level or `\addcontentsline` shift — no unrelated movement.

## Out of scope

`hw1/` fixtures are **not** regenerated: `hw1/solutions.txt:541` (`List ::= nil | join <<...>>`) hits an unrelated parse error — `join` now lexes as the relational-algebra keyword and breaks the free-type definition. Pre-existing on `main`; tracked separately.

## Delegation

rmh (engine + tests), mdm (CLI help), ghr (docs), adb (fixtures). jms not consulted — typographic hierarchy, not Z semantics.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

Follow-up fix to the merged three-level-TOC work. A post-merge Copilot review found two real defects in the `generate_document` pre-scan that sets `self._toc_depth`. Write-set: ONLY `src/txt2tex/latex_gen.py` and `tests/test_11_text_blocks/test_toc_three_levels.py`. TDD: write failing tests first, show red, implement, show green, `make check` green.

Background on current code (in `latex_gen.py` `generate_document`, ~line 481-489): there is a pre-scan that loops over `ast.items`, and on the first `Contents` node sets `self._toc_depth = toc_depth_from_keyword(_item.depth)`, then `if self.toc_parts: self._toc_depth = 3`. `self._toc_depth` is initialised to 3 only in `__init__`. `_generate_contents` (in `codegen/text_blocks.py`) now reads `self._toc_depth` (do NOT change that file).

Two defects:
1. **State leak across reuse.** Because `_toc_depth` is only assigned when a `Contents` node is found, a `LaTeXGenerator` reused for a second `generate_document()` keeps the prior document's depth (or the `toc_parts` bump). It must reset per call.
2. **Nested `CONTENTS:` ignored.** The pre-scan only inspects top-level `ast.items`. A `CONTENTS:` directive parsed inside a `Section`/`Solution`/`Part` is missed, so its depth keyword is silently dropped (and `_generate_contents` no longer reads `node.depth`, so nothing recovers it).

Fix in `generate_document`:
- BEFORE the pre-scan, reset `self._toc_depth = 3` unconditionally (default) so each call starts clean.
- Replace the top-level-only loop with a recursive, document-order (pre-order DFS) search for the FIRST `Contents` node anywhere in the tree — descending into the `.items` of `Section`, `Solution`, and `Part` nodes. On finding it, set `self._toc_depth = toc_depth_from_keyword(node.depth)` and stop.
- Keep the `if self.toc_parts: self._toc_depth = 3` bump AFTER the search.
- Add a small private helper for the recursive search (e.g. `_find_contents_depth(items) -> int | None` returning the first keyword-derived depth, or a node-finder). Keep it typed, no `Any`, follow the file's existing style and the project's strict-typing rules.

First VERIFY the parser actually produces nested `Contents` nodes: write a quick check (in the test or a scratch assertion) that `CONTENTS: 3` inside a `=== Section ===` parses into a `Contents` node within `Section.items`. If the parser does NOT nest it (keeps it top-level), say so in your report and make the nested test reflect actual parser behaviour — but still implement the recursive walk (harmless and future-proof) and keep the reset.

Tests to add in `test_toc_three_levels.py`:
- **Reuse isolation:** one `LaTeXGenerator` instance; call `generate_document` on a doc with `CONTENTS: 1`, then on a SECOND doc that has `**`/`(a)` but NO `CONTENTS:` directive. Assert the second document's output has `_toc_depth` reset to default 3 — e.g. the part `\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{…}` IS present in doc 2 (it would be absent if depth 1 leaked). Also assert doc 2's output equals a fresh-generator run on the same source.
- **Nested CONTENTS depth honored:** a doc with `CONTENTS: 3` (or `full`) nested inside a `=== Section ===`, assert `\setcounter{tocdepth}{3}` and all three `\addcontentsline` levels present (adjust to actual parser nesting behaviour if it differs).
- Keep existing tests green.

Report the red→green evidence, whether the parser nests `Contents`, and confirm `make check` is green. Do NOT touch docs — ghr handles the stale USER_GUIDE line separately.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reuse isolation (defect 1)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestReuseIsolation:
    """A reused LaTeXGenerator must not leak _toc_depth across calls.

    The first document sets depth 1 via CONTENTS: 1.  The second document
    has no CONTENTS: directive, so it must revert to the default depth of 3
    — meaning all three addcontentsline levels are emitted.
    """

    _DOC1 = "CONTENTS: 1\n\n=== Title ===\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"
    _DOC2 = "=== Title ===\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"

    def _parse_ast(self, src: str) -> object:
        lexer = Lexer(src)
        tokens = lexer.tokenize()
        return Parser(tokens).parse()

    def test_second_call_subsubsection_present(self) -> None:
        # If depth leaks, this is absent because depth 1 was set by doc1.
        gen = LaTeXGenerator()
        gen.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC1))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        latex2 = gen.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC2))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex2

    def test_second_call_subsection_present(self) -> None:
        gen = LaTeXGenerator()
        gen.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC1))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        latex2 = gen.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC2))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Q1}" in latex2

    def test_second_call_matches_fresh_generator(self) -> None:
        # The reused generator's second output must equal a fresh generator's output.
        gen_reused = LaTeXGenerator()
        gen_reused.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC1))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        latex_reused = gen_reused.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC2))  # type: ignore[arg-type]

        gen_fresh = LaTeXGenerator()
        latex_fresh = gen_fresh.generate_document(self._parse_ast(self._DOC2))  # type: ignore[arg-type]

        assert latex_reused == latex_fresh


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nested CONTENTS: (defect 2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestNestedContentsDepth:
    """CONTENTS: inside a Section must still set _toc_depth.

    Verifies that the parser nests the Contents node inside Section.items

    """

    _SRC = "=== Introduction ===\n\nCONTENTS: 3\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"

        # Confirm structural assumption: Contents is inside Section.items.
        lexer = Lexer(self._SRC)

class TestFragmentTocDepth:
    """generate_fragment (REPL/preview) must honor CONTENTS: and not leak depth.

    It shares _resolve_toc_depth with generate_document, so CONTENTS: depth is
    applied and _toc_depth resets per call.
    """

    _DOC1 = "CONTENTS: 1\n\n=== Title ===\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"
    _DOC2 = "=== Title ===\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"
    _DOC3 = "CONTENTS: 3\n\n=== Title ===\n\n** Q1 **\n\n(a) content\n"

    def _parse_ast(self, src: str) -> Document:
        ast = Parser(Lexer(src).tokenize()).parse()
        assert isinstance(ast, Document)
        return ast

    def test_fragment_honors_contents_depth(self) -> None:
        # CONTENTS: 3 in a fragment must set tocdepth 3 and emit all levels.
        latex = LaTeXGenerator().generate_fragment(self._parse_ast(self._DOC3))
        assert r"\setcounter{tocdepth}{3}" in latex
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex

    def test_fragment_does_not_leak_depth(self) -> None:
        # Reused generator: depth 1 fragment then a no-CONTENTS fragment must
        # revert to default 3 (subsubsection present), not leak depth 1.
        gen = LaTeXGenerator()
        gen.generate_fragment(self._parse_ast(self._DOC1))
        latex2 = gen.generate_fragment(self._parse_ast(self._DOC2))
        assert r"\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{(a)}" in latex2

tool_input.prompt:
Fix a confirmed parser bug: a single-line relational-algebra `group` expression emits a spurious `\\` line break (and a trailing `\quad`) into inline math.

Reproduction: `X == R group (Sum(a) as b)` generates `$X == R \mathop{\mathrm{Group}}(\mathrm{Sum}(a)~\mathrm{as}~b) \\` + `\quad $`. The `\\` inside inline `$…$` is invalid and causes odd line spacing.

Root cause — `src/txt2tex/parser_pkg/expressions.py`, the GROUP branch (around lines 1926–1959). After `_parse_group_rhs` consumes the entire `group (…)` expression, the branch checks the next token for a line continuation:

```python
has_continuation = False
if self._match(TokenType.CONTINUATION):
    self._advance()
    has_continuation = True
    if self._match(TokenType.NEWLINE):
        self._advance()
    self._skip_newlines()
elif self._match(TokenType.NEWLINE):     # ← BUG
    has_continuation = True
    self._skip_newlines()
else:
    self._skip_newlines()
if has_continuation:
    # rebuilds GroupAggregate/Group with line_break_after=True
```

A bare `NEWLINE` here is just the end of the line (the group RHS is already fully parsed), not a continuation. Treating it as one sets `line_break_after=True`, and the codegen (`codegen/algebra.py` `_generate_group_aggregate` / `_generate_group`) appends ` \\\n\quad `.

Fix: in the GROUP branch ONLY, remove the bare-`NEWLINE`→`has_continuation` case so that only an explicit trailing `\` (TokenType.CONTINUATION) sets `line_break_after`. I.e. collapse the `elif self._match(TokenType.NEWLINE): …` into the `else: self._skip_newlines()`. Do NOT touch the Divide/Join branches or any other operator — those check for continuation *before* parsing a right operand, so a newline there is a genuine operand continuation; the GROUP branch is different because it checks *after* the full expression.

Write-set: ONLY `src/txt2tex/parser_pkg/expressions.py` and a test file under `tests/`. TDD, every step shown:
1. Write failing tests FIRST (assert on exact fragments):
   - `X == R group (Sum(a) as b)` → generated LaTeX line for X contains `\mathop{\mathrm{Group}}` but does NOT contain `\\` and does NOT contain `\quad`.
   - Same for a two-aggregate single-line group `R group (Sum(a) as b, Sum(c) as d)`.
   - Same for the regroup form `R group ({a, b} as g)` on one line — no `\\`.
   - Regression: an explicit continuation — `R group (Sum(a) as b, \` then newline then `Sum(c) as d)` — STILL sets the break (preserve existing opt-in behavior); assert the `\\` IS present. (If the explicit-continuation path is hard to express in a test, at minimum assert it is unchanged from current behavior — do not remove that capability.)
   - A non-group regression: a single-line `R join S` inside a Restrict, and a `pi`/`sigma` line, are unaffected (no new/lost `\\`).
2. Run the new tests; SHOW them failing (the single-line ones fail today because `\\` is emitted).
3. Implement the one-branch fix.
4. Run the tests; SHOW them passing.
5. `make check` to ZERO violations; SHOW the green tail. Update any existing test that asserted the old bare-newline group-break behavior (if one exists) — note which you changed and why.

Report red→green evidence, the diff, and confirm `make check` is green. Verify independently with `make -C <repo> check` semantics (run from the repo root). Do NOT touch docs, the codegen, or other parser branches.

tool_input.content:
"""Regression tests: single-line GROUP must not emit a spurious line break.

A bare NEWLINE after a GROUP's closing ')' is just the end of the line —
it is not a continuation marker.  Treating it as one sets line_break_after=True
on the AST node and the codegen appends ' \\\\\n\\quad ' into inline math,
producing invalid LaTeX.

See: expressions.py GROUP branch, ~line 1936.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from txt2tex.ast_nodes import Document, Expr, GroupAggregate
from txt2tex.latex_gen import LaTeXGenerator
from txt2tex.lexer import Lexer
from txt2tex.parser import Parser


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers (mirror the pattern in test_group_aggregators.py)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _lex(src: str) -> list:
    return Lexer(src).tokenize()


def _expr(src: str) -> Expr:
    result = Parser(_lex(src)).parse()
    item: Expr = result.items[0] if isinstance(result, Document) else result  # type: ignore[assignment]
    return item


def _expr_latex(src: str) -> str:
    """Generate LaTeX for a standalone expression (no document wrapper)."""
    gen = LaTeXGenerator(use_fuzz=True)
    return gen.generate_expr(_expr(src))


def _doc_latex(src: str) -> str:
    """Generate the full document LaTeX for a complete document source."""
    tokens = Lexer(src).tokenize()
    ast = Parser(tokens).parse()
    return LaTeXGenerator().generate_document(ast)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bug: single-line group with trailing newline must NOT emit \\ or \quad
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_single_line_group_aggregate_no_line_break() -> None:
    r"""R group (Sum(a) as b) followed by \n must not emit \\ or \quad.

    The trailing newline is a statement terminator, not a continuation.
    """
    src = "R group (Sum(a) as b)\n"
    result = _expr_latex(src)
    assert r"\mathop{\mathrm{Group}}" in result
    assert r"\\" not in result
    assert r"\quad" not in result


def test_abbreviation_group_aggregate_no_line_break_in_inline_math() -> None:
    r"""X == R group (Sum(a) as b) in a document must emit $…$ with no \\ inside.

    This is the exact reproduction case from the bug report.
    """
    src = "TITLE: probe\n\nX == R group (Sum(a) as b)\n"
    latex = _doc_latex(src)
    # The inline-math span must contain the Group operator
    assert r"$X == R \mathop{\mathrm{Group}}" in latex
    # A \\ inside inline math is invalid — must not appear
    assert r"\\\\" not in latex
    assert r"\quad" not in latex


def test_two_aggregate_single_line_no_line_break() -> None:
    r"""R group (Sum(a) as b, Sum(c) as d) on one line must not emit \\."""
    src = "R group (Sum(a) as b, Sum(c) as d)\n"
    result = _expr_latex(src)
    assert r"\mathop{\mathrm{Group}}" in result
    assert r"\\" not in result
    assert r"\quad" not in result


def test_regroup_form_single_line_no_line_break() -> None:
    r"""R group ({a, b} as g) on one line must not emit \\."""
    src = "R group ({a, b} as g)\n"
    result = _expr_latex(src)
    assert r"\mathop{\mathrm{GROUP}}" in result
    assert r"\\" not in result
    assert r"\quad" not in result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AST: line_break_after must be False for plain single-line group
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_single_line_group_aggregate_ast_no_line_break_flag() -> None:
    """Parsing a single-line group sets line_break_after=False on the AST node."""
    src = "R group (Sum(a) as b)\n"
    node = _expr(src)
    assert isinstance(node, GroupAggregate)
    assert node.line_break_after is False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regression: explicit CONTINUATION token after ) still sets the break
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_explicit_continuation_after_group_still_breaks() -> None:
    r"""An explicit backslash continuation after GROUP's ')' still sets \\."""
    # Source: "R group (Sum(a) as b) \<newline>"  — the \ is the CONTINUATION token
    src = "R group (Sum(a) as b) \\\n"
    result = _expr_latex(src)
    assert r"\mathop{\mathrm{Group}}" in result
    assert r"\\" in result


def test_explicit_continuation_ast_line_break_flag_true() -> None:
    r"""Explicit \ continuation after GROUP sets line_break_after=True on the AST."""
    src = "R group (Sum(a) as b) \\\n"
    node = _expr(src)
    assert isinstance(node, GroupAggregate)
    assert node.line_break_after is True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Non-group regressions: join and project are unaffected
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_join_single_line_unaffected() -> None:
    r"""R join S on a single line: no spurious \\ added by this fix."""
    src = "R join S\n"
    result = _expr_latex(src)
    assert r"\mathrm{Join}" in result
    # A single-line join should not have a line break injected
    assert r"\\" not in result


def test_project_single_line_unaffected() -> None:
    r"""pi [a, b] R on a single line: no spurious \\ added by this fix."""
    src = "pi [a, b] R\n"
    result = _expr_latex(src)
    # Project emits \pi or \Pi; confirm no stray line break
    assert r"\\" not in result

tool_input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head fix/group-spurious-linebreak --title "fix(algebra): no spurious line break after single-line group" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

A single-line relational-algebra `group (…)` expression emitted a stray `\\` and `\quad` into the inline math, e.g.:

```
$X == R \mathop{\mathrm{Group}}(\mathrm{Sum}(a)~\mathrm{as}~b) \\
\quad $
```

The `\\` is invalid inside inline `$…$` and produced odd vertical spacing.

## Cause

In `parser_pkg/expressions.py`, the GROUP branch of the operator loop parses the **entire** `group (…)` RHS, then checks the next token for a continuation. A bare end-of-line `NEWLINE` was treated as a continuation, setting `line_break_after=True`; the codegen then appended ` \\\n\quad `.

This differs from `Divide`/`Join`, which check for a continuation *before* their right operand — there a newline genuinely means "operand continues on the next line." GROUP checks *after* its full expression, so a bare newline is just a statement terminator.

## Fix

In the GROUP branch only, a bare newline counts as a continuation **only when a chaining relational operator follows** (`join`, `div`, `cross`, `group`, `ungroup`). An explicit trailing `\` still forces the break. No other operator branch is touched.

## Tests (`tests/test_group_no_spurious_linebreak.py`)

- Single-line group — aggregate, two-aggregate, and regroup forms — emit no `\\`/`\quad`.
- AST `line_break_after` is `False` for a plain single-line group.
- Explicit `\` continuation still sets the break (LaTeX + AST).
- `join`/`project` single lines unaffected.

`make check` green (4817 passed, 3 expected xfails). Verified on the originating assignment: the `Group` lines now close cleanly with `$`.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

---
name: feedback-coursework-hints
description: When Jim is working through his own coursework/assignment, give error counts + stage/category hints, never the fix or corrected code
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When Jim is solving his own coursework (e.g. the DAT assignment relational-algebra answers), he does NOT want direct answers. Give:

- the **number of errors**,
- **which stage/line** each is at,
- optionally a **category** (e.g. "name doesn't resolve" vs "runs but selects wrong rows" vs "grouping partition"),

and stop there. Do NOT state the fix, the corrected expression, or the specific token to change.

**Why:** he is learning the material and wants to find and fix the errors himself; spoon-feeding defeats the purpose.

**How to apply:**
- Default to a per-stage scorecard (stage | count | category) plus a total.
- Affirm what's correct (e.g. "the ranking structure is sound") — that's useful signal, not a fix.
- Only give the actual answer if he explicitly asks for it afterwards.
- This is the opposite of the earlier C1 traces where full row-by-row answers WERE wanted — gate on whether he's asking to understand vs. asking to self-check his own work.

Related: [[feedback-response-length]] (answer + stop), [[feedback-verification-bar]].

"""Tests for extend operator and two-argument aggregate form.

Features under test:
- Two-arg aggregator: Agg(rel, attr) as alias  (Date SUM(rel, exp) form)
- extend operator: R extend (Agg(...) as alias, ...)
- Fuzz routing: extend abbreviation goes to inline math, not zed
- Regression: single-arg aggregate and group output unchanged
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from txt2tex.ast_nodes import (
    Aggregator,
    AggregatorClause,
    Document,
    Expr,
    ExtendAggregate,
    GroupAggregate,
    Identifier,
)
from txt2tex.latex_gen import LaTeXGenerator
from txt2tex.lexer import RESERVED_WORDS, Lexer
from txt2tex.parser import Parser
from txt2tex.tokens import Token, TokenType


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _lex(src: str) -> list[Token]:
    """Tokenize src."""
    return Lexer(src).tokenize()


def _expr(src: str) -> Expr:
    """Parse a single expression and return the first document item."""
    result = Parser(_lex(src)).parse()
    item: Expr = result.items[0] if isinstance(result, Document) else result  # type: ignore[assignment]
    return item


def _expr_latex(src: str) -> str:
    """Generate LaTeX for an expression (math content without document wrapper)."""
    gen = LaTeXGenerator(use_fuzz=True)
    item = _expr(src)
    return gen.generate_expr(item)


def _doc_latex(src: str) -> str:
    """Generate LaTeX for a full document source string."""
    tokens = Lexer(src).tokenize()
    ast = Parser(tokens).parse()
    return LaTeXGenerator().generate_document(ast)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lexer: extend keyword
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_lex_extend_token() -> None:
    """extend is lexed as EXTEND token, not IDENTIFIER."""
    tokens = _lex("extend")
    assert tokens[0].type == TokenType.EXTEND


def test_extend_in_reserved_words() -> None:
    """extend appears in RESERVED_WORDS."""

    assert isinstance(doc_result.items[1], Abbreviation)
    assert doc_result.items[1].name == "G"

def _parse_aggregator_clause(self) -> AggregatorClause:
        """Parse a single ``Count(attr) as alias`` or ``Sum(rel, attr) as alias`` clause.

        the first identifier inside the parens.  First arg becomes ``source_rel``,
        second arg becomes ``attr``.  Single-arg form leaves ``source_rel=None``.
        """
        agg_tok = self._current()
        if agg_tok.type not in self._AGGREGATOR_TOKEN_TYPES:
            raise ParserError(
                f"Expected aggregator keyword (Count, Sum, Avg, Min, Max, Median), "
                f"got {agg_tok.type.name} ({agg_tok.value!r})",
                agg_tok,
            )
        agg = self._TOKEN_TO_AGGREGATOR[agg_tok.type]
        self._advance()  # consume aggregator keyword
        if not self._match(TokenType.LPAREN):
            raise ParserError(
                f"Expected '(' after '{agg_tok.value}' in aggregator clause",
                self._current(),
            )
        self._advance()  # consume '('
        if not self._is_attr_name_token():
            raise ParserError(
                f"Expected attribute name inside '{agg_tok.value}(...)'",
                self._current(),
            )
        first = self._advance().value
        # Two-arg form: Agg(source_rel, attr) as alias
        source_rel: str | None = None
        if self._match(TokenType.COMMA):
            self._advance()  # consume ','
            if not self._is_attr_name_token():
                raise ParserError(
                    f"Expected attribute name after ',' in '{agg_tok.value}({first}, ...)'",
                    self._current(),
                )
            source_rel = first
            attr = self._advance().value
        else:

        if not self._match(TokenType.RPAREN):
            raise ParserError(
                f"Expected ')' after attribute in '{agg_tok.value}({attr})'",
                self._current(),

        self._advance()  # consume ')'
        if not self._match(TokenType.AS):
            cur = self._current()
            raise ParserError(

                f"got {cur.type.name} ({cur.value!r})",

            raise ParserError(
                f"Expected alias name after 'as' in '{agg_tok.value}({attr}) as ...'",
                self._current(),

            attr=attr,
            alias=alias,
            source_rel=source_rel,
            line=agg_tok.line,
            column=agg_tok.column,

"""Tests for extend operator and two-argument aggregate form.

Features under test:
- Two-arg aggregator: Agg(rel, attr) as alias  (Date SUM(rel, exp) form)
- extend operator: R extend (Agg(...) as alias, ...)
- Fuzz routing: extend abbreviation goes to inline math, not zed
- Regression: single-arg aggregate and group output unchanged
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from txt2tex.ast_nodes import (
    Abbreviation,
    Aggregator,
    Document,
    Expr,
    ExtendAggregate,
    GroupAggregate,
    Identifier,
)
from txt2tex.latex_gen import LaTeXGenerator
from txt2tex.lexer import RESERVED_WORDS, Lexer
from txt2tex.parser import Parser
from txt2tex.tokens import Token, TokenType


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _lex(src: str) -> list[Token]:
    """Tokenize src."""
    return Lexer(src).tokenize()


def _expr(src: str) -> Expr:
    """Parse a single expression and return the first document item."""
    result = Parser(_lex(src)).parse()
    item: Expr = result.items[0] if isinstance(result, Document) else result  # type: ignore[assignment]
    return item


def _expr_latex(src: str) -> str:
    """Generate LaTeX for an expression (math content without document wrapper)."""
    gen = LaTeXGenerator(use_fuzz=True)
    item = _expr(src)
    return gen.generate_expr(item)


def _doc_latex(src: str) -> str:
    """Generate LaTeX for a full document source string."""
    tokens = Lexer(src).tokenize()
    ast = Parser(tokens).parse()
    return LaTeXGenerator().generate_document(ast)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lexer: extend keyword
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_lex_extend_token() -> None:
    """extend is lexed as EXTEND token, not IDENTIFIER."""
    tokens = _lex("extend")
    assert tokens[0].type == TokenType.EXTEND


def test_extend_in_reserved_words() -> None:
    """extend appears in RESERVED_WORDS."""
    assert "extend" in RESERVED_WORDS


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 1: Two-arg aggregate parse
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_two_arg_agg_parse_sum() -> None:
    """R group (Sum(a, b) as t) -> AggregatorClause(SUM, source_rel='a', attr='b')."""
    node = _expr("R group (Sum(a, b) as t)")
    assert isinstance(node, GroupAggregate)
    assert len(node.clauses) == 1
    clause = node.clauses[0]
    assert clause.agg == Aggregator.SUM
    assert clause.source_rel == "a"
    assert clause.attr == "b"
    assert clause.alias == "t"


def test_two_arg_agg_parse_count() -> None:
    """R group (Count(rel, x) as total) -> source_rel='rel', attr='x'."""
    node = _expr("R group (Count(rel, x) as total)")
    assert isinstance(node, GroupAggregate)
    clause = node.clauses[0]
    assert clause.agg == Aggregator.COUNT
    assert clause.source_rel == "rel"
    assert clause.attr == "x"
    assert clause.alias == "total"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 2: Two-arg aggregate render
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_two_arg_agg_render_sum() -> None:
    r"""Two-arg Sum renders as \mathrm{Sum}(a, b)~\mathrm{as}~t."""
    result = _expr_latex("R group (Sum(a, b) as t)")
    assert r"\mathrm{Sum}(a, b)~\mathrm{as}~t" in result


def test_two_arg_agg_render_full_date_example() -> None:
    r"""Date example: Sum(payments, amountPaid) as totalInvoicePayment."""
    result = _expr_latex(
        "R group (Sum(payments, amountPaid) as totalInvoicePayment)"
    )
    assert (
        r"\mathrm{Sum}(payments, amountPaid)~\mathrm{as}~totalInvoicePayment"
        in result
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test 3: Single-arg aggregate unchanged (regression)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_single_arg_agg_source_rel_is_none() -> None:
    """R group (Sum(x) as t) -> source_rel is None."""
    node = _expr("R group (Sum(x) as t)")
    assert isinstance(node, GroupAggregate)
    clause = node.clauses[0]
    assert clause.source_rel is None
    assert clause.attr == "x"
    assert clause.alias == "t"

## What

Adds C. J. Date's **`extend`** operator and the **two-argument aggregate** `Agg(rel, attr)` to the relational-algebra family, so a relation-valued attribute (RVA) can be aggregated correctly.

## Why

Projecting to `(key, amount)` then `Sum(amount)` **deduplicates equal values** under set semantics and undercounts — two equal payments on one invoice collapse to one row before the sum. The correct pattern preserves multiplicity:

```
InvPayGrouped == Payment group ({paymentId, amountPaid} as payments)   # nest distinct tuples
PaidPerInv    == InvPayGrouped extend (Sum(payments, amountPaid) as totalInvoicePayment)
```

`group` nests (reduces cardinality); `extend` consumes an RVA and adds a per-tuple scalar (preserves it). That's Date's GROUP vs EXTEND distinction.

## Changes

- **Two-argument aggregate** `Agg(rel, attr)` in the aggregator clause — `Sum(payments, amountPaid)` → `\mathrm{Sum}(payments, amountPaid)`. Second arg is an attribute name. Single-arg form unchanged (distinct arity).
- **`extend` operator** — new keyword; `R extend (Agg(rva, attr) as alias, …)` → `R \mathop{\mathrm{Extend}}(…)`.
- **Fuzz routing** — `ExtendAggregate` added to the DAT expression set, so `extend` renders as inline math and is never routed into a fuzz-checked `zed` block (per the earlier `cross` fuzz-routing fix).

## Notation

Reviewed by **jms**: two-argument aggregate is Date's `SUM(r, exp)` form; rendering `\mathrm{Sum}(payments, amountPaid)~\mathrm{as}~alias` is byte-consistent with the existing single-arg clause. The GROUP-vs-EXTEND choice (option b: add a proper `extend`) is recorded in `docs/DESIGN.md` (ADR). The two-arg form is accepted in any aggregate clause but its correct home is `extend`.

## Tests

`tests/test_extend_aggregate.py` — 20 tests: two-arg parse/render (Sum, Count), single-arg regression (unchanged, `source_rel is None`), `extend` parse/render (single + multi-clause), **inline-routing** (an `extend` abbreviation renders `$…$`, not `\begin{zed}`), and no-spurious-linebreak.

`make check` green (4837 passed, 3 expected xfails). Verified the worked pipeline renders to spec and stays out of fuzz.

## Docs

DESIGN ADR, CHANGELOG (Added), and USER_GUIDE (two-arg form, `extend`, and a `group` vs `extend` comparison with the worked example).
EOF

tool_input.prompt:
Read-only consult on a txt2tex parser bug in the Z set-comprehension bullet disambiguation. I need your judgment on the correct rule, not an implementation — rmh will implement.

## The bug

A nested set comprehension inside a comprehension's predicate breaks the OUTER comprehension's bullet (`@`/spot) detection. Concretely, this input:

```
# { c : Case | c.managerId = m.managerId land
    (#({cp : CaseParticipant | cp.caseId = c.caseId}) >= 2) land
    c.hasBeenReviewed = zFalse . c.propertyId } > 5
```

The outer comprehension is `{ c : Case | <pred> . c.propertyId }` — predicate, then bullet `.`, then characteristic expression `c.propertyId`. txt2tex emits `zFalse.c.propertyId` (a field-selection chain on `zFalse`) instead of `zFalse @ c.propertyId` (bullet + characteristic expression). fuzz then correctly rejects it: "Argument of selection must have schema type — Expression: zFalse.c, Arg type: zBool".

WITHOUT the nested comprehension the same line parses correctly (`zFalse @ c.propertyId`) and type-checks. The nested `{cp : ... | ...}` is the sole trigger.

## Root cause (confirmed by reading the parser)

`src/txt2tex/parser_pkg/expressions.py`. The bullet-vs-selection decision (line ~2338) is:
`if self._in_comprehension_body and next_token.value in self._current_quantifier_vars:` → treat `.` as the bullet separator (Z RM §3.16: a declared comprehension variable after a dot begins the characteristic expression, it is not a field selector).

Each of the 4 comprehension-parse sites (lines 818/876, 1049/1080, 1158/1169, 1510/1533) does:
- `prev_quantifier_vars = self._current_quantifier_vars` ; set to this comp's vars ; **restored** in `finally`.
- `self._in_comprehension_body = True` ; but the `finally` sets it back to **`False` unconditionally** — it is never saved.

So `_current_quantifier_vars` is correctly stacked (save/restore), but `_in_comprehension_body` is NOT. When the NESTED comprehension finishes, its `finally` sets `_in_comprehension_body = False`, clobbering the OUTER comprehension's `True`. The outer parser then sees `_in_comprehension_body == False` at the `. c.propertyId` position, so the bullet check fails and `.` is parsed as selection.

## Proposed fix

At each of the 4 sites: save `prev_in_comprehension = self._in_comprehension_body` before setting it `True`, and in the `finally` restore `self._in_comprehension_body = prev_in_comprehension` instead of assigning `False`. (This makes the flag a properly nested stack, matching how `_current_quantifier_vars` is already handled.)

## Questions for you (Z semantics / parser correctness)

1. Is save/restore of `_in_comprehension_body` the correct model — i.e. the bullet disambiguation should key off the INNERMOST enclosing comprehension being in-body, and on exit revert to the enclosing scope's state? I believe yes, but want your confirmation against Z RM §3.16.

2. `_current_quantifier_vars` is currently **replaced** (not unioned) with the inner comp's variables while parsing the inner body, then restored. So inside the inner body only inner vars are "declared"; a selection on an outer var (e.g. `cp.caseId = c.caseId`, where `c` is the outer var) is correctly treated as a genuine field selection `c.caseId`, not a bullet. Is REPLACE correct, or should the disambiguation see the UNION of all enclosing comprehension variables? Give a concrete Z example where replace-vs-union changes the parse, if one exists (e.g. a nested comprehension whose characteristic expression legitimately begins with an outer-scope variable). If union is needed for correctness, say so — rmh will implement whichever you specify.

3. Any other edge cases this class of bug implies: bullet in the inner comprehension while the outer also has a bullet; a nested comprehension appearing in the characteristic expression (after the outer bullet) rather than the predicate; the constrained-quantifier double-pipe form (`forall x : T | c | b`). Which of these must be in the regression test set?

Return: (a) confirm/correct the fix rule, (b) replace vs union verdict with a justifying example, (c) the list of nested-comprehension shapes that must be regression-tested. Cite Z RM sections where they bear on the answer.

Mission: fix a Z set-comprehension parser bug where a NESTED comprehension in a predicate breaks the OUTER comprehension's bullet (`@`/spot) detection. Branch `fix/nested-comprehension-bullet` is already checked out. TDD, strict steps, `make check` clean before returning.

Write-set (only these two files):
- `src/txt2tex/parser_pkg/expressions.py`
- `tests/test_nested_comprehension_bullet.py` (new)

## The bug (reproduce first)

Input `{ c : Case | <pred containing #({cp : CaseParticipant | cp.caseId = c.caseId})> land c.hasBeenReviewed = zFalse . c.propertyId }` emits `zFalse.c.propertyId` (a field-selection chain) instead of `zFalse @ c.propertyId` (bullet + characteristic expr). fuzz then rejects: "Argument of selection must have schema type — Expression: zFalse.c, Arg type: zBool". WITHOUT the nested comprehension, the same line correctly emits `@`. The nested `{cp : ... | ...}` is the sole trigger.

A full reproduction file is at `.tmp/mgr.txt` (run `uv run txt2tex .tmp/mgr.txt --tex-only` — it fails at fuzz with the zFalse.c error; the generated `.tmp/mgr.tex` line shows `zFalse.c.propertyId`).

## Root cause (confirmed by jra + jms; do not re-litigate)

`expressions.py`. The bullet-vs-selection decision (line ~2338) is:
`if self._in_comprehension_body and next_token.value in self._current_quantifier_vars:` → treat `.` as the bullet separator.

Four comprehension/quantifier parse sites do save/restore of `_current_quantifier_vars` but NOT of `_in_comprehension_body`:
- 818/876, 1049/1080, 1158/1169, 1510/1533.

At each: `_current_quantifier_vars` is saved to a `prev_quantifier_vars` local and restored in `finally`; but `_in_comprehension_body` is set `True` and the `finally` assigns it `False` **unconditionally** (never saved). So when a NESTED comprehension's `finally` runs, it clobbers the OUTER comprehension's `True` → the outer bullet check fails.

## The fix — two changes, applied at all four sites

### Change 1 — stack `_in_comprehension_body` (jms verdict a)
At each of the 4 sites, before setting `self._in_comprehension_body = True`, save the prior value:
`prev_in_comprehension = self._in_comprehension_body`
and in the `finally`, RESTORE it instead of assigning False:
`self._in_comprehension_body = prev_in_comprehension`
IMPORTANT: line 873 (and its siblings) deliberately set the flag `False` mid-parse before parsing the post-bullet characteristic expression — LEAVE those in place. Only the `finally` assignment changes from `= False` to `= prev_in_comprehension`. Use a distinct local name per site (they're separate scopes).

### Change 2 — UNION `_current_quantifier_vars` across nesting (jms verdict b)
An inner comprehension is in the scope of ALL enclosing schema-text variables. Currently sites 819/1159/1511 REPLACE: `self._current_quantifier_vars = set(variables)`. Change to UNION with the enclosing scope:
`self._current_quantifier_vars = prev_quantifier_vars | set(variables)`
Site 1050 already reads `prior_vars | set(variables)` (union within one schema-text's `;`-chained bindings); make it also union the enclosing scope: `prev_quantifier_vars | prior_vars | set(variables)`. The `finally` restore to `prev_quantifier_vars` is already correct and unchanged.
This does NOT regress the reported case (the post-dot tokens there are field labels `caseId`/`propertyId`, in no variable set). It DOES fix the case where an inner comprehension's characteristic expression begins with an outer-scope variable.

## Tests — `tests/test_nested_comprehension_bullet.py`, written FIRST and shown failing

Assert on the ACTUAL emitted LaTeX fragment (per project TDD rule — not "does `@` appear somewhere"). For each shape, extract the comprehension body and assert the bullet renders as `@` at the correct position AND that the broken selection chain (`zFalse.c` / the outer var chained onto the predicate's last token) is ABSENT. Where practical also assert fuzz acceptance is not the vehicle — keep these as generator/parser unit tests on the emitted string so they run without the fuzz binary. (You may add one integration test that runs the full pipeline on `.tmp`-style input and asserts type-check passes, guarded like existing fuzz-dependent tests.)

jms specified 7 shapes; implement all. 1, 3, 6 are load-bearing; 2, 5 are the guards a naive fix trips:
1. Nested comprehension in the outer predicate, outer bullet after it (the reported bug). Expect `@ c.propertyId`; NOT `zFalse.c.propertyId`.
2. Nested comprehension in predicate, NO outer bullet (characteristic tuple defaults to the declaration). Outer must still parse cleanly to `}`.
3. Inner comprehension with explicit bullet whose characteristic expression is an OUTER-scope variable — jms's example shape `{ c : Case | c.ok . { cp : Part | cp.ref = c.id . c } }`. Under the OLD replace logic the inner `. c` mis-parses as selection; under union it's the inner bullet. Assert the inner `@ c` (bullet) renders, not `(c.id).c`.
